A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same REASONINGCOMPILER study, with readable text, equations, figures, tables, and Appendices A–G. Pages 2–20 match in both extracted text and rendered appearance. V3 appends a NeurIPS checklist.

before.justification: V2 reports original compiler evaluations in Section 4 and Appendices B–G, including speedups, sample efficiency, ablations, API costs, and proposal fallback rates.

after.justification: V3 retains the same original experimental results in Section 4 and Appendices B–G. Its additional checklist does not introduce further experiments.

M1.justification: The LLM proposal generation, validation and fallback procedures, hardware cost model, and MCTS algorithm remain unchanged in Section 3 and Appendices A and G. The checklist restates the LLM's existing role.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate the same five layer benchmarks and end-to-end Llama-3-8B across five hardware platforms. The checklist's reference to six benchmarks describes this retained coverage.

E2.justification: The corresponding comparisons retain TVM MetaSchedule with evolutionary search and unguided MCTS. The LLM choices compared in Figure 4 and Table 4 are also unchanged.

E3.justification: Section 4.1 retains the same TVM version, GPT-4o mini configuration, branching factor, exploration parameter, hardware environments, and measurement procedures. The checklist introduces no new or revised experimental protocol.

E4.justification: The LLM-choice, historical-context, and branching-factor ablations remain identical, as does the proposal-validity analysis in Appendix G. The checklist adds qualifications without new robustness tests or supplementary analyses.

E5.justification: Both versions already state in Section 4.1 that experiments are repeated 20 times and averaged. Checklist item 7 repeats this information without adding uncertainty estimates, seed information, or statistical testing procedures.

E6.justification: Figures 3–4 and Tables 1–8 retain all result entries and associated findings. For example, Table 1 still reports a 5.0× geometric-mean speedup and a 10.8× sample-efficiency gain.

T1.justification: The optimization objective, MDP formulation, UCT equation, and conditional asymptotic-optimality discussion remain unchanged. Checklist item 3 adds a characterization of the work's theoretical scope, without revising the mathematics or supplying proofs.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same claims about LLM-guided MCTS, optimization without retraining, improved sample efficiency, and model-serving benefits. The checklist affirms these existing contributions.

C2.justification: Checklist item 2 explicitly identifies API cost/access concerns, limited benchmark coverage, and possible degradation under context-length or interpretability constraints. Item 3 also newly characterizes the paper as making no theoretical claims requiring proofs, despite the retained Section 2 optimality discussion.

D1.justification: Checklist items 5 and 8 newly identify setup/run instructions and the README in the already-linked repository. Item 12 explicitly identifies TVM's Apache License 2.0. These are disclosure additions; the PDFs establish no change to code availability or implementation.

R1.justification: Section 5 and the 61 research references remain unchanged. The checklist reuses existing TVM citations and adds administrative policy links without changing research positioning or novelty claims.

P1.justification: V3 appends a standalone, 16-item NeurIPS checklist and changes the first author's displayed name from Sujun Tang to Annabelle Sujun Tang. The existing narrative, section order, and Appendices A–G are unchanged.

P2.justification: V3 adds checklist pages formatted with numbered questions, answers, and bulleted guidelines, alongside small first-page author/header edits. Existing Figures 1–4, Tables 1–8, captions, and page layouts on pages 2–20 are visually identical.

improvement.justification: V3 modestly improves transparency through explicit limitations, licensing information, and documentation pointers. However, checklist item 3's denial of proof-requiring theoretical claims is difficult to reconcile with Section 2's asymptotic-optimality assurance, while item 7 affirms statistical-significance reporting using only the existing averaging statement. These gains and reporting inconsistencies leave the net quality effect unclear; the underlying scientific evidence is unchanged.
